flashcard_questions.a: The increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities.

flashcard_questions.q: When did more people first live in urban areas than in rural areas?
What proportion of the world's population is projected to live in cities by 2050?
How many people lived in urban areas in 2005?
How many people are expected to live in urban areas by 2050?
What is a megacity in geography?
flashcard_questions.a: A city with a population of more than 10 million people.

flashcard_questions.q: How many megacities were there worldwide in 2020?
How many megacities are predicted worldwide by 2050?
Which city is the world's largest megacity, with around 37 million people?
What is the population of the megacity of Delhi?
What is rural-urban migration in geography?
flashcard_questions.a: The movement of people from the countryside into towns and cities.

flashcard_questions.q: What is natural increase in a population?
flashcard_questions.a: When the birth rate is higher than the death rate.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do cities in LICs have high rates of natural increase?
flashcard_questions.a: Many of the migrants arriving are young adults of childbearing age.

flashcard_questions.q: What share of the population in HICs already lives in cities?
Which Nigerian city has grown into a megacity?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term-to-definition (urbanisation, megacity, rural-urban migration, natural increase), 9 case-study-to-fact carrying one figure each and naming the place or year (2007 landmark, 70% by 2050, 3.4 and 6.5 billion, 34 and 50 megacities, Tokyo, Delhi, 80% in HICs), 1 cause-to-consequence (young migrants drive natural increase), 1 named example (Lagos). The UN's 10 new megacities by 2030 and the push/pull factor lists were trimmed; push and pull factors were left out because any card on them would ask for a list.
